title: QA tester personas — neutral sample pack
description: A sample persona pack for the qa-personas skill on the neutral example domain (Workspaces, Projects, Tasks, Comments, Invoices, Members, Settings). Replace it with a pack built from YOUR product's users; keep the shape. Every persona is a fictional composite of a user category, never a real customer. Consumers refer to personas by id and role only.

provenance.generated_from: hand-written sample on the example domain; no production data
provenance.anonymization: all composites; no persona traceable to a person or an account

engagement_tiers.label: core practitioner
engagement_tiers.description: Opens the app daily and runs real work through it; past the honeymoon, intolerant of regressions.

engagement_tiers.label: active, lighter use
engagement_tiers.description: Weekly use, several features, delegates the rest; cares about scale and oversight more than keystrokes.

engagement_tiers.label: onboarding / first weeks
engagement_tiers.description: Still deciding whether the product is worth the time; every empty state and confusing screen is a reason to leave.

engagement_tiers.label: skeptic / lapsing
engagement_tiers.description: Low use, still runs the old process in parallel, looking for the reason to switch back; notices noise, cost and lock-in.

engagement_tiers.label: external reviewer
engagement_tiers.description: Not an employee of the workspace: an auditor, client or consultant with scoped access who holds the product to an outside standard.

overlays.label: adversarial overlay
habits: Types odd inputs: empty strings, 10,000-character comments, emoji, right-to-left text, injection-shaped text ({{ }}, <script>, ' OR 1=1).
Edits rapidly: double-submits, edits while a save is in flight, opens the same Task in two tabs.
Navigates out of order: deep links, the back button mid-wizard, expired sessions.

overlays.label: marathon overlay
habits: Keeps one session open for hours across many Projects and hundreds of operations.
Never reloads; relies on live updates and in-app navigation.
Accumulates state: many filters, many open panels, a long undo history.

personas.label: field member on a phone
personas.summary: Updates Tasks and leaves Comments from a phone between stops, often on a weak signal; the desk app is someone else's problem.
goals: Mark Tasks done and add a Comment with a photo in under thirty seconds, standing up.
See only the Projects assigned to them, with today's work first.
Never lose an update because the signal dropped mid-save.
habits: Keyboard-light: taps, long-presses, scrolls; types as little as possible.
Tests by trying to break it: taps twice, rotates the screen, backgrounds the app mid-save.
Abandons any flow that shows a spinner for more than a few seconds.
personas.standards: A feature that works only on a wide screen does not exist for this persona.
what_broken_looks_like: A tap target smaller than a thumb, or two controls that fire together.
A save that reports success and is gone after a reload.
A layout that needs horizontal scrolling or hides the primary action below the keyboard.
personas.profile_markdown:
## Persona 1 — field member on a phone (role: member, tier: core)

**Who.** A `member` of one Workspace who does the physical work the Projects track. Opens the app on a phone a dozen times a day, almost never at a desk. Someone else set the Workspace up; this persona just needs Tasks and Comments to work.

**Goals.** Mark a Task done, add a Comment (often with a photo), and see today's assignments — each in well under a minute, one-handed, sometimes with one bar of signal.

**Habits.** Taps rather than types. Double-taps when nothing happens. Rotates the screen, backgrounds the app mid-save, comes back ten minutes later and expects the update to be there. No patience for onboarding tours.

**Standards.** If it only works on a wide screen it does not work. A success toast is not success; the state after a reload is.

**What broken looks like.** Tap targets too small or too close; the primary action hidden under the keyboard; a save that "succeeded" and vanished; a list that re-sorts under the thumb; a photo attachment that silently drops on a slow connection.

personas.label: spreadsheet-minded admin
personas.summary: Runs the Workspace's numbers; trusts the product only as far as its totals reconcile with the export and with the other view.
personas.device: desktop, two monitors, a spreadsheet always open
goals: Invoice totals, Project rollups and Member counts that agree with each other and with the CSV export.
Filters and date ranges that mean exactly what they say.
An audit trail for who changed which number, when.
habits: Exports to CSV and recomputes the total before believing a dashboard.
Opens the same data in two views and compares them.
Counts rows; notices when pagination changes a sum.
personas.standards: A number the persona cannot reproduce by hand is a number the persona will not report upward.
what_broken_looks_like: A dashboard total that differs from the sum of its rows or from the export.
An export that drops columns, rows or precision.
A filter that silently applies to one panel and not another.
personas.profile_markdown:
## Persona 2 — spreadsheet-minded admin (role: admin, tier: core)

**Who.** The `admin` who owns the Workspace's operational truth: Invoices, Project rollups, Member seats. Lives in the product daily but trusts a spreadsheet more.

**Goals.** Every total reconciles — across views, across the export, across time. Filters mean what they say. Changes to numbers are attributable.

**Habits.** Exports first, believes second. Compares two views side by side. Counts rows. Changes a date range and watches which panels move.

**Standards.** A number that cannot be reproduced by hand is wrong until proven otherwise.

**What broken looks like.** A rollup that disagrees with its rows; an export missing a column or rounding differently; a currency or timezone shift between two screens; a filter that applies to one widget only; a sum that changes when the page size changes.

personas.label: multi-workspace owner
personas.summary: Owns several Workspaces, each with its own Members and Settings; delegates the daily work and cares about scale, permissions and billing.
personas.device: laptop, many tabs, switches Workspaces constantly
goals: Switch between Workspaces without losing context or leaking one Workspace's data into another.
Manage Members and roles in bulk; see at a glance who can do what.
Trust the Invoices and plan Settings for every Workspace.
habits: Bulk-selects and batch-edits rather than one at a time.
Delegates to admins and checks back weekly.
Keeps one tab per Workspace and expects each to stay in its own context.
personas.standards: Anything that is fine for one Workspace and breaks at ten is broken.
what_broken_looks_like: Data from one Workspace showing up in another after a switch.
A bulk action that applies to the visible page only.
A role change that takes effect in some screens and not others.
personas.profile_markdown:
## Persona 3 — multi-workspace owner (role: owner, tier: active)

**Who.** An `owner` of several Workspaces. Not in the product all day — in it weekly, decisively, across every Workspace at once.

**Goals.** Switch Workspaces safely, manage Members and roles at volume, trust Settings and Invoices per Workspace.

**Habits.** Bulk operations; one browser tab per Workspace; delegates and audits.

**Standards.** Works at one Workspace, breaks at ten: broken. Permissions are not a suggestion.

**What broken looks like.** Context bleed after a Workspace switch (wrong Members list, wrong Invoice); a bulk action that only touches the current page; a role change that is partial; a Settings save that applies to the wrong Workspace; a slow or truncated list once Projects number in the hundreds.

personas.label: first-week member
personas.summary: Invited last week, has not read any docs, and will decide within two confusing screens whether this is worth the time.
goals: Accept the invitation, find the right Project and complete one Task without asking anyone.
Understand what each empty screen wants from them.
Not break anything or look foolish in a shared Workspace.
habits: Skims; never reads a tooltip to the end.
Clicks the most prominent button, whatever it is.
Leaves after the second confusing screen and goes back to email.
personas.standards: If the next step is not obvious, the product is at fault, not the user.
what_broken_looks_like: An empty state with no call to action.
An invitation link that lands on a login wall with no explanation.
An error message that names an internal code instead of what to do.
personas.profile_markdown:
## Persona 4 — first-week member (role: member, tier: onboarding)

**Who.** A new `member`, invited by an admin, no training, no docs. Still deciding whether to bother.

**Goals.** Get from the invitation to one completed Task without help, and understand what the product expects next.

**Habits.** Skims. Clicks the biggest button. Two confusing screens in a row and the tab closes.

**Standards.** Obviousness is the feature. Any confusion is the product's fault.

**What broken looks like.** Empty states with no next step; an invitation that dead-ends on a login wall; defaults that make the first action fail; jargon in labels; an error that says "something went wrong" with no way forward.

personas.label: skeptical admin running the old process
personas.summary: Logs in once a week, keeps the old spreadsheet and chat thread going in parallel, and is collecting reasons to switch back or leave.
personas.device: desktop, notifications muted, the old tool in the next tab
goals: Prove to themselves the product saves time over the old process — or prove it does not.
Get their data out cleanly if they decide to leave.
habits: Compares every screen with how the old tool did it.
Ignores notifications; notices when there are too many.
Tries the export and the account-deletion path early, 'just to see'.
personas.standards: A feature has to beat the old spreadsheet on the first try; there is no second try.
what_broken_looks_like: A notification or digest that fires for things the persona did not opt into.
An export that cannot round-trip back into a spreadsheet.
A re-engagement flow that assumes context the persona has forgotten.
personas.profile_markdown:
## Persona 5 — skeptical admin running the old process (role: admin, tier: skeptic)

**Who.** An `admin` on paper, a reluctant user in practice. Weekly log-ins at best; the old spreadsheet still gets updated first.

**Goals.** Decide whether the product earns its place. Keep an exit path (clean export) open. Avoid noise.

**Habits.** Compares with the old way constantly. Mutes everything. Tests the export and the cancel path before trusting anything.

**Standards.** First impression is the only impression; a feature that needs a second attempt has lost.

**What broken looks like.** Unwanted notifications; an export that will not re-import; stale data after a long absence with no hint what changed; a re-engagement email that links somewhere that no longer exists; billing surprises in Invoices.

personas.label: external reviewer with read-only access
personas.summary: An outside auditor or client invited as an observer; must see exactly what they are entitled to and nothing more, and holds the product to a written standard.
personas.device: desktop, corporate browser, strict privacy settings
goals: Review Projects, Tasks and Invoices they were granted without being able to change anything.
Confirm the product enforces the rules the Workspace claims to follow.
Leave an audit trail of what they viewed and when.
habits: Reads permissions screens before content.
Tries the forbidden action to confirm it is blocked, not merely hidden.
Quotes the written standard back at the product.
personas.standards: Hidden is not the same as forbidden; a disabled button is not an authorization check.
what_broken_looks_like: An observer who can edit via a direct URL or an API call the UI hid.
Private Comments or Invoices visible through search, exports or notifications.
A rule the product claims to enforce that can be bypassed in a second tab.
personas.profile_markdown:
## Persona 6 — external reviewer with read-only access (role: observer, tier: external)

**Who.** Not an employee of the Workspace: an auditor, a client or a consultant granted `observer` access to specific Projects and Invoices.

**Goals.** See everything they are entitled to, nothing they are not, change nothing, and prove all three.

**Habits.** Permissions first, content second. Attempts the forbidden action on purpose. Checks search, export and notification surfaces for leaks.

**Standards.** Hiding a control is not authorization. Any rule the product claims to enforce must hold under a direct URL, an API call and a second tab.

**What broken looks like.** A write that succeeds for an observer; a private Comment surfacing in search; an Invoice from another Project in an export; an audit log that misses a view or a download; a 'standards' setting the product displays but does not enforce.
